Hi Sam — good catch, and sorry for the friction.

We’ve seen Calendly default to the organizer time zone in a few browser/cookie combos, so some visitors still see US times even when they’re in APAC. Two quick options that should work right away:

1) Manual pick: I’ll propose a UTC time below (so it’s unambiguous) and send a calendar invite with the correct SGT tz.
2) Calendly workaround: append the tz parameter to the link like this: https://calendly.com/redwood/demo?tz=Asia/Singapore — that forces the page to render in the requested zone.

Proposed time (all converted):
- 2026-08-14 13:00 UTC = 21:00 SGT = 09:00 PDT (same day)
- 2026-08-14 14:00 UTC = 22:00 SGT = 10:00 PDT

I’m attaching a short agenda and I’ll also create a direct .ics invite to avoid any Calendly ambiguity. If those UTC slots look good, tell me which one and I’ll send the invite that includes the explicit time zone metadata.

Notes / best-practice summary for the procurement & scheduling team:
- Use a canonical timezone (we use UTC for cross-region demos) and include local equivalents in the invite body.
- Prefer direct .ics/Google invites over third-party scheduling UI when participants span >2 regions. Calendly/Chili Piper are great for self-serve but can be brittle at DST boundaries or with strict cookie/privacy settings.
- If you must share a scheduling link, append the tz query param (e.g., ?tz=Europe/Berlin or ?tz=Asia/Singapore) to force rendering.
- For recurring or long-term meetings, pin the event timezone in the calendar app (Google/GCal allows setting event timezone explicitly).
